> Thanks!
> 
> I think exposing this via `OpenXRInterface` is fine. My initial thought would have been to expose it as a normal singleton (ie `Engine::get_singleton()->add_singleton(...)`) but we're currently doing a thing where we don't create the singleton if OpenXR isn't enabled, and that would be super weird as a global singleton.
> 
> So, either this, or expose it as a normal singleton that's created always

I think I'm in favor of exposing via a singleton as this would remove the strict dependency on Godot 4.7 and allow us to integrate the feature into the current major version of the vendors plugin.

> > Thanks!
> > I think exposing this via `OpenXRInterface` is fine. My initial thought would have been to expose it as a normal singleton (ie `Engine::get_singleton()->add_singleton(...)`) but we're currently doing a thing where we don't create the singleton if OpenXR isn't enabled, and that would be super weird as a global singleton.
> > So, either this, or expose it as a normal singleton that's created always
> 
> I think I'm in favor of exposing via a singleton as this would remove the strict dependency on Godot 4.7 and allow us to integrate the feature into the current major version of the vendors plugin.

I don't think this new approach matches the intent of my comment since `extension_api.json` still needs to be updated in order for the plugin to see and make use of `virtual void on_register_metadata(OpenXRInteractionProfileMetadata *p_interaction_profile_metadata);` thus introducing a strong dependency on Godot 4.7.

Can't we instead register `OpenXRInteractionProfileMetadata` as a singleton and access it from the vendors plugin, with the expectation that the singleton will be null when running against 4.6, but non-null when running against 4.7? 

> My initial thought would have been to expose it as a normal singleton (ie Engine::get_singleton()->add_singleton(...)) but we're currently doing a thing where we don't create the singleton if OpenXR isn't enabled, and that would be super weird as a global singleton.

@dsnopek Can you elaborate on why this would be an issue?

> > My initial thought would have been to expose it as a normal singleton (ie Engine::get_singleton()->add_singleton(...)) but we're currently doing a thing where we don't create the singleton if OpenXR isn't enabled, and that would be super weird as a global singleton.
> 
> @dsnopek Can you elaborate on why this would be an issue?

This would indeed be an issue unless we always instantiate this class even when OpenXR is not enabled.
Else things like documentation and json creation will ignore the fact that this class is exposed as a singleton because it is only exposed if it has been registered.

I really wish we could just expose the `get_singleton` static method instead of this crazy singleton registration system from a bygone era.

@m4gr3d Apologies, I meant to write this comment at the end of the day yesterday but it got away from me. I believe exposing `OpenXRInteractionProfileMetadata` via `Engine::get_singleton()->add_singleton(...)` could be done, here's what I've found. Please let me know your thoughts!

In order for the `OpenXRInteractionProfileMetadata` singleton to be available in GDExtension at the time `_on_register_metadata` runs, the singleton needs to be added during the core initialization step (and yes, it would also need to always be initialized regardless on if OpenXR is enabled). All of the extension classes in core that register metadata would then also need to be moved from the server to the core initialization step as well, since `OpenXRInteractionProfileMetadata` relies on the extensions being registered when it's created.

Chatting with @dsnopek he made the observation that, since `_on_register_metadata` exists only for this interaction profile case, it really makes the most sense to just have that function hand off the singleton, that way we don't have to actually expose it, and I agree with this approach.

So, I believe we could go with your preferred approach if we always instantiate the class and register the singleton, as well as move all initialization of the class and relevant extensions to the core level. Or we could go with the approach currently implemented in the PR, which I personally prefer, but does introduce a 4.7 dependency.

> Chatting with @dsnopek he made the observation that, since `_on_register_metadata` exists only for this interaction profile case, it really makes the most sense to just have that function hand off the singleton, that way we don't have to actually expose it, and I agree with this approach.

Yeah, if we ignore what existed before, I feel like passing `OpenXRInteractionProfileMetadata *` to `_on_register_metadata()` is probably the right design for this particular virtual method. If we could go back in time to when this API was created, that would probably have been the right design to begin with.

That said, depending on how clever we want to get, I think we could still come up with a way to build `godot_openxr_vendors` such that the virtual method is provided in a build that works with Godot 4.6, but is only "active" when loaded in Godot 4.7+. This may be as simple as updating the `extension_api.json` to include the new version of the virtual method? But, even if that doesn't work, I think it'd still be possible by directly interacting with the low-level GDExtension interface (this sort of thing just isn't a feature of godot-cpp).

@m4gr3d I've updated https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_openxr_vendors/pull/474 with an `extension_api.json` hack. While `XR_ANDROID_mouse_interaction` will still require 4.7+, godot cpp will not need to be updated. Tested and works as expected on 4.6 and this PR. Let me know your thoughts!
